title: Stability Lighthouse Catalog and Ops Decision Brief
content:
Purpose:
This is a working catalog + quick decision brief to translate our product-level KPIs into deterministic ops actions during staged rollouts and surge scenarios. The doc is intentionally terse — the goal: 1) map observable signals to simple runbook steps, 2) provide throttles/fallbacks that can be executed by on-call or traffic ops without deep product context, 3) capture experiment knobs for product + infra to iterate.

High-level summary (one-paragraph):
We call this a 'Lighthouse' because each feature/cohort pair should emit a small set of signals (latency p95, error rate, model-quality SLI, cost-per-1k-tokens) and have 3 pre-approved responses (gentle throttle, degrade to smaller model variant, full hold-and-rollback). This brief catalogs recommended thresholds and decision heuristics for the next two betas (beta-a / beta-b) and an unconstrained public ramp.

Immediate ask:
- Product + Eng: confirm owners for the 6 features listed below by EOD Fri.
- SRE/Infra: wire beta-a to the throttle policy defined in section 'Throttle matrix'. Feature flags and routing tags are in PRODOPS-721.
- CS: prepare canned messaging for customers if we apply variant fallback to dedicated customers.

Signals and KPIs (what we observe):
- Latency p95 (ms): server-side generation time for text responses (excludes client RTT). Primary signal for UX degradation.
- Request error rate (%): 5xx and model-failure responses combined. Primary reliability SLI.
- Quality regression (QA fail %): fraction of sampled responses failing the nightly prompt-set sanity checks (automated eval).
- Cost per 1K tokens ($): used to gate cost-driven throttles for non-enterprise cohorts.
- Queue depth / request backlog: immediate indicator of saturation for batchers.

Stability lighthouse entries (catalog):
1) feature: contextual-summaries | cohort: beta-a (internal) | owner: Marcus Liu
   signals: latency p95, error rate, QA-fail
   primary threshold (warning): p95 > 800ms OR error_rate > 1.0% OR QA-fail > 4%
   critical threshold: p95 > 1400ms OR error_rate > 2.5% OR QA-fail > 8%
   recommended action (warning): reduce concurrency cap by 20%, enable small-model fallback on 10% traffic, notify #product-ops
   recommended action (critical): 50% traffic reroute to small-model variant, pause new user invites, open incident channel

2) feature: chat-threads-v2 | cohort: beta-b (select customers) | owner: Sana Patel
   signals: queue depth, latency p95, cost/1k tokens
   primary threshold: queue depth > 1200 OR p95 > 700ms OR cost > $12/1k
   critical threshold: queue depth > 2000 OR p95 > 1200ms OR cost > $20/1k
   recommended action (warning): enable short-turn caching for prefix traces, reduce token cap per response by 10%
   recommended action (critical): throttle background batching to favor low-latency paths, enable routing to dedicated pool, grade-rollback to previous model version for the cohort

3) feature: emb-rerank-ml | cohort: internal-sli-tests | owner: Jonah Reyes
   signals: model-failure %, rerank precision drop (A/B test metric)
   thresholds: precision drop > 6% OR model-failure > 1.2% -> immediately switch to last-known-good weights, mark commit for rollback, run offline batch eval

4) feature: multimodal-probe | cohort: limited-preview | owner: Priya Mehta
   signals: GPU OOM alarms, infra errors, quality regressions for image prompts
   thresholds: any OOM or infra error spike > 0.3% -> drain to low-memory pool, reduce sequence lengths, temporarily disable multimodal attachments for the cohort

Throttle matrix (ops knobs):
- gentle-throttle: factor 0.8 concurrency cap, 10% rollout attenuation to fallback model, set lower token cap (default -10%)
- mid-throttle: factor 0.6 concurrency cap, 50% traffic reroute to fallback model, lower token cap (-25%), enable prefix caching aggressively
- hard-hold: 0% increase (freeze new sessions), 75% traffic reroute to fallback, pause invites and marketing for cohort

Decision heuristics (succinct):
- If any primary threshold is hit for > 5 minutes AND trending worse for an additional 5 minutes -> apply gentle-throttle.
- If any critical threshold is hit OR two different primary thresholds are hit simultaneously -> escalate to mid-throttle + open incident.
- If mid-throttle fails to reduce critical signals in 10 minutes -> hard-hold and rollback.
- For quality regressions (QA-fail): prefer fallback to a previous model snapshot rather than throttling UX unless cost or infra signals accompany the regression.

Quick runbook (for on-call):
1) Confirm signal via observability dashboard (link pinned to #prod-ops). Is it a real-time spike or a steady drift?
2) Run the small checklist: a) check model variant health, b) check batching queue depth, c) inspect most recent deploys (git tags shown in infra PR link).
3) Apply gentle-throttle via policy api: /internal/throttle/apply {policy: gentle-throttle, feature_tag: X} and annotate incident.
4) If no improvement in 10m escalate to mid-throttle and email CS owners.
5) If quality regression choose model-snapshot fallback path (follow PRODOPS-721 runbook).

Rollout knobs recommended for product experiments:
- default traffic ramp: 0.5% -> 2% -> 10% -> 25% -> 50% -> 100% (min 1 hour per step unless stability gates pass faster)
- early gating: require p95 < 600ms and QA-fail < 2% to move beyond 10% step
- cost gate for public: projected cost/1k tokens < $8 for consumer tiers or require finance signoff

Owner & contact matrix (who presses which buttons):
- apply throttles / routing policies: Infra-SRE (oncall) (pager: infra-oncall)
- model fallback switches: Applied-ML team (owner listed per feature)
- customer comms (for select customers): CS escalation lead (cc: product-ops)
- final go/no-go at 25% step for public: product director sign-off (delegated to product-ops lead during off hours)

Open questions / TODOs:
- Need to define exact prefix caching TTLs and metrics for cache hit ratio; infra suggests 30s/60s vs 5m — decision needed (Marcus).
- Who owns the canonical QA prompt set? current repo is under research/qa-evals; want product to add targeted prompts for each feature (Sana).
- Confirm cost thresholds for enterprise vs consumer tiers (finance).
- Add synthetic traffic probe that runs sample prompts at ramp boundaries to detect regressions faster.

Notes to self / friction we expect:
- Small-model fallback helps UX for latency but can mask quality regressions — add an explicit QA-fail annotation when fallback triggers so we don't silently ship degraded quality.
- Ops needs a single button to revert routing to previous snapshot; current process touches multiple services. Tracking GH issue infra#789.

Appendix: quick cheat sheet (copyable to pager/incident):
- Gentle throttle: policy gentle-throttle -> reduce concurrency 20% -> notify #product-ops
- Mid throttle: policy mid-throttle -> 50% traffic to fallback -> open incident -> call product owner
- Hard hold: policy hard-hold -> freeze invites -> route 75% to fallback -> exec rollback if QAs still fail

Last revision notes: 2025-02-02: updated thresholds after circadian traffic test on 2025-01-28 (see PRODOPS-721 notes); added the cost gate for public ramp.

If you want a one-pager export for the on-call rotation board, I can trim this to the top table and the 5-line runbook — ask in thread.
